title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll Steps Down After 18 Months Amid Reported Tensions With Hegseth
detail: The White House said Tuesday, September 1, 2026, that Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down after 18 months on the job, becoming the latest senior military leader to depart during the Trump administration. No official reason was given; an Army official said Driscoll spoke with Trump about the state of the Army and submitted his resignation. Widely reported tensions between Driscoll — the youngest-ever Army secretary and a close friend of Vice President JD Vance — and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had grown since Hegseth ousted Driscoll ally Gen. Randy George in April and rolled back a drone-modernization program Driscoll had championed. A White House spokeswoman praised Driscoll as 'highly effective in advancing President Trump's agenda.'

media.caption: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll steps down amid reported friction with Defense Secretary Hegseth

title: Trump Nominates Hung Cao as Permanent Navy Secretary
detail: President Trump announced Tuesday, September 1, 2026, via Truth Social that he is nominating Hung Cao — a Vietnamese-refugee-turned-Navy-veteran who has served as acting Navy secretary since April 2026 — to the permanent post, calling him 'a true warrior' and urging the Senate to 'confirm this Warfighter, ASAP.' Cao, a Naval Academy graduate and former special operations diver and explosive-ordnance-disposal officer who deployed to Iraq, Afghanistan, and Somalia before an unsuccessful 2024 Senate run against Tim Kaine, took over the acting role after John Phelan was removed. His stated priorities are personnel readiness, shipbuilding, and the sixth-generation F/A-XX fighter program; Senate confirmation is still required.

media.caption: Trump nominates acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao to the permanent post

title: House Passes Stopgap Funding Bill, Averting Pre-Midterm Shutdown Through Dec. 11
detail: The House voted 370-48 on Tuesday, September 1, 2026 to pass a continuing resolution funding the federal government through December 11, 2026, averting a shutdown at the September 30 fiscal-year deadline just weeks before the midterm elections. The Senate had already passed the measure, sending it to Trump's desk for signature. Speaker Mike Johnson said Congress would 'avoid the threat' of a shutdown; the stopgap includes provisions blocking OMB's proposed rule on federal grants and preventing fund transfers to Border Patrol. Congress has not completed any of the 12 full-year appropriations bills for fiscal year 2027.

media.caption: Speaker Mike Johnson after the House passed a stopgap funding bill averting a pre-election shutdown
